key_insight: Learning to sample from a Gibbs reward distribution can achieve logarithmic-in-time sampling regret at fixed temperature, unlike the typical square-root scaling of classical regret.
engineering_relevance: The framework informs uncertainty-aware sampling for entropy-regularized reinforcement learning, RLHF, and reward-guided generation where diverse, high-quality outputs matter.
method: Define sampling regret using temperature-normalized cumulative KL divergence to the unknown Gibbs target.
Develop sampling analogues of UCB and Thompson sampling: UCS and TS².
Bound regret through squared confidence widths and unified frequentist and Bayesian decompositions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical logarithmic-regret guarantees in standard settings and new posterior-random Gibbs bounds, but no empirical evaluation.
watch_item: Logarithmic guarantees hold at fixed temperature in standard settings; practical Gibbs sampling costs and temperature dependence require scrutiny.
paper_title: The Tilted Sampling Problem: Optimism, Posterior Sampling, and Logarithmic Regret
